text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG aims to transform its existing bilateral airline partnerships into a multilateral alliance, Friedel Roedig, Lufthansa's executive president, alliances, told the airline's in-house newspaper Lufthanseat.
On February 12, airline officials told Reuters that up to nine airlines were planning to launch a "seamless airline product" under a single brand name in May.

Roedig told the company newspaper "Our alliance system currently consists of a sum of bilateral partnerships. Because the world has become a global arena, we must find a way from these bilateral partnerships into a multilateral alliance."
A strong alliance would improve profitability and counter future threats from other airlines, he added.

"We must really see our alliance structure as an offensive step into the future and as our way towards profitable progress. The defensive part of our alliance will equip us to counter future threats," said.
"We must assume that the proposed and immensely strong alliance between British Airways and American Airlines will come about," he said.

"If we want to withstand its impact we must continue even more determinedly the course we have adopted. As an airline, we must meet the needs arising from globalisation and position ourselves with competitive network earnings for the future. That is our way into the 21st century," Roedig said.
Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber was quoted by the company newspaper as saying that a common marketing strategy for the alliance would be presented in May.
It would have a common frequent flyer programme and close co-operation on sales, electronic ticketing, passenger services and cargo, they forecast.

On February 12, airline officials told Reuters that the alliance would include Lufthansa AG, United Airlines, Air Canada, Scandinavian Airline System, Thai International Airways, Varig and possibly British Midland.
Roedig said Lufthansa was considering how to expand the alliance in the Asia-Pacific region since this could not be covered by a single partner.
"We must ponder how we are going to operate in the market in China and stay in the Japanese market, talks are also being conducted in Australia and New Zealand," Roedig said.

The Lufthansa nwspaper reported that Weber had said in a recent speech to sales staff that a common marketing strategy for the Lufthansa alliances would be presented in May. No further details were given.
SAS said on February 14 that it was seeking closer co-operation with its airline partners.
